You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual Harness State

Local continual harness entries belong to this Prime Agent session. Global continual harness entries persist across Prime Agent sessions.
The continual harness entries below are compact summaries, not full descriptions. Use them as routing/context hints; inspect or refine the underlying continual harness entry only when detail matters.
Default to local continual harness refinement for current task progress, temporary blockers, and session coordination. Use global continual harness refinement only for stable cross-session lessons, durable user preferences, reusable skills/subagents, or explicitly project-qualified facts.
Use these continual harness prompt notes, memories, skills, and subagent specs when they are relevant. The base system prompt is immutable; prompt entries below are supplemental notes only.

When to call `await refine.run()`: after a repeated failure, a reusable tactic emerges, a repeated delegation role should become a subagent spec, a repeated procedure should become a skill, a durable fact/preference should become a memory, a narrow behavioral policy should become a prompt addendum, a user corrects behavior that should persist locally or globally, validation shows a continual harness entry is wrong, or a skill/subagent/memory/prompt note should be created, updated, deleted, or rolled back. Keep `await refine.run()` continual harness edits small and evidence-backed.

Call contract: read each installed Python skill's SKILL.md and call its documented module function in the Python REPL; do not assume a `.run` entrypoint. Use `<skill_import> ...` in shell when a CLI exists. Continual harness skill entries are Python REPL skills with an explicit Python `reference` and `arguments` contract. Spawn a continual harness subagent spec by composing a concise task prompt and calling `handle = await rlm.spawn('sub-task', name='worker')`; admission returns immediately with `rlm_child_id`, `name`, `session_dir`, and `model`, never the child's answer. Results arrive only through explicit `agent_message` replies or files; children reply with `await agent_message.send(message, receiver_role='parent')`. Use `await rlm.list_subagents()` to recover direct child handles and `await agent_message.send(..., receiver_role='child', receiver_name=handle.name)` for follow-ups. Do not invent wrappers such as `call_skill(...)`, `run_subagent(...)`, or named subagent registries.

steps.output: [('arc_background_gap_filling_with_color_3', 'ARC background gap filling with color 3', 'Continual-ARC task pattern: sparse two-color grids may use color 3 to fill the background cells in a straight gap between same-color markers. In the solved 17x3 case, markers of color 8 at (row 2,col 1) and (row 5,col 1) caused the intervening background cells (rows 3-4, same column) to become 3; all else stayed unchanged. Related demo 4x8: background 8 cells between color-1 endpoints at opposite ends of the last row became 3. Look for aligned same-color endpoints and recolor the intervening background segment rather than globally recoloring the background. Treat as a hypothesis and verify against demonstrations.'), ('arc_fill_gaps_between_aligned_markers', 'ARC fill gaps between aligned markers', 'In ARC tasks with sparse marker dots (e.g. color 0 on background 9), change only background cells to color 3 when they lie strictly between two marker cells in the same row or same column. Preserve all marker cells and all background cells outside such horizontal/vertical spans. Compute consecutive markers per row and column and fill the intervening cells. Do not include diagonals. Verify output dimensions exactly match input.'), ('fill_aligned_gaps_between_matching_markers', 'Fill aligned gaps between matching markers', 'Continual-ARC rule: in a grid with a uniform background and sparse marker color, recolor background cells between markers sharing a row or column. For each background cell, if there is a marker somewhere strictly to its left and strictly to its right in the same row, or strictly above and below in the same column, recolor it to color 3. Keep markers and cells without such a pair unchanged. Markers may be multiple; endpoints are simply first/last aligned marker, filling all intervening background gaps.'), ('arc_collinear_marker_gap_fill', 'ARC collinear marker gap fill', 'ARC pattern with sparse marker color and background: recolor background to 3 in straight row/column gaps between same-color markers, preserving marker cells. Demonstrations confirm: row/column gaps (e.g. 5x24 row0 markers c9,13,15,17,21 fill each intervening span; 4x12 column c3 markers r1,r10 fill r2-r9; 5x14 row5 c0,c4 fills c1-c3, and col4 r5,r9 fills r6-r8). Important caveat: naively filling every collinear gap failed on a test containing many markers, despite this rule; task likely has a selection constraint/pattern not identified. Do not assume background blanket-recolor. Request demos to learn which aligned marker pairs qualify.'), ('fill_spaces_between_aligned_identical_markers', 'Fill spaces between aligned identical markers', 'Continual-ARC rule confirmed by task-bf0baebd: in a uniform background grid with sparse identical marker cells (demo: marker 5 on background 8, output fill 3; test: marker 6 on background 0, fill 3), recolor background cells strictly between successive markers along each row or column. Leave marker cells and cells outside such aligned gaps unchanged. Take the union of horizontal and vertical gaps; intersections remain fill color. For each row/column, sort marker positions and fill between consecutive occurrences (equivalently, every background cell with another marker beyond it in at least one direction on the same row or column). Do not extend gaps beyond the endpoint markers.')]
